sources.title: de Sitter Black Holes, Schottky Peaks, and Continuous Heat Engines

evidence.text: Sample a 150×150 parameter grid, numerically compute horizon quantities and mine the data along selected curves for temperature derivatives. Coordinates are (a/m,m²Λ) or (Q/m,m²Λ); analytical derivatives across the full domain are described as difficult.

sources.title: Heat and work in black hole thermodynamics via holography

evidence.text: Auxiliary fields resolve the double-trace deformation in the path integral. Large-N saddle-point variation yields mixed conditions Φ̂(s) + w + vΠ(b) = 0 and Φ̂(b) + vΠ(s) = 0, where Π is the on-shell action derivative with respect to the boundary field.

sources.title: The Volume of 2-D black holes

evidence.text: Motivate a dilaton-weighted volume measure from the X dependence of the Euclidean action and Gibbons–Hawking term. Import the entropy result obtained by first-law and Wald techniques to fix the corresponding area interpretation.

sources.title: Black holes and entropy

evidence.text: Compare the work recovered while lowering a heavy box with the work needed to retrieve it after radiation has reduced its mass. The horizon energy assigned to each box mass determines the net efficiency.

sources.title: de Sitter Black Holes, Schottky Peaks, and Continuous Heat Engines

evidence.text: Use a truncated harmonic-oscillator specific-heat series to illustrate Schottky-like behavior, and an imported three-level maser model with Boltzmann populations to motivate continuous-engine thermodynamics. Horizon first laws supply the black-hole heat/work bookkeeping.

sources.title: Heat and work in black hole thermodynamics via holography

evidence.text: Constrained maximization of von Neumann entropy gives a product coarse-grained state: ρ̄(s) ∝ exp[−β(H*(s) − μO)] and ρ̄(b) ∝ exp[−BH*(b)]. Multipliers reproduce the exact state's accessible expectation values; O need not commute with H*(s).

sources.title: The Volume of black holes

evidence.text: Can stationary spacetimes admit a thermodynamically meaningful volume independent of stationary slicing, and can discrete identifications produce bounded horizon area with unbounded volume?
